- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot after sharp spikes in the history (e.g., 74–76 range), then fail to correct downward.
- Mean reversion is underappreciated — model holds too much upward bias after recent highs, ignoring the tendency to revert to lower levels.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the second half of the 30-day window, suggesting model struggles with long-term trend decay.
- Model exhibits lagged response to recent price drops — fails to adjust downward quickly when true prices fall sharply.
- Overshoots are more common after high historical values (e.g., 76+), suggesting model overreacts to recent volatility.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of downward corrections after spikes — often misses the “drop after peak” pattern.
- Forecasts show persistent upward bias even when true prices are trending downward — suggests model lacks downward momentum calibration.
